facts.raw_span: A ten-month-old Hispanic girl presented for evaluation of facial asymmetry noted since birth
the right lower lip deviates inward, whereas the rest of facial movement is symmetric
Pregnancy was uncomplicated, and the patient was born full term
Developmental milestones are appropriate for age
her face is symmetric at rest
When she smiles, the right lower lip deviates inward
frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth are symmetric on both sides
A neurodevelopmental examination is normal
Magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals is normal
echocardiography shows no cardiac anomalies
an auditory brainstem response test reveals normal hearing pathways

concepts.why: The patient's right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying, indicating a congenital unilateral lower lip palsy.
Although the patient's facial movement is mostly symmetric, the deviation of the right lower lip when smiling or crying could be a mild manifestation of Moebius syndrome.
The patient's right lower lip deviation when smiling or crying could be a result of a peripheral facial palsy, although the lack of other symptoms makes this less likely.
The patient's facial asymmetry and deviation of the right lower lip when smiling or crying could be part of a broader craniofacial anomaly, such as hemifacial microsomia.
The patient's right lower lip deviation when smiling or crying could be an isolated congenital facial paresis, without other associated anomalies.

The inward deviation of the right lower lip when smiling or crying, despite normal facial movement at rest and normal results from magnetic resonance imaging, echocardiography, and auditory brainstem response tests, points towards a specific issue with the lower lip.

rationales.F02: The right lower lip deviates inward, which is a key feature of congenital unilateral lower lip palsy and isolated congenital facial paresis.
rationales.F06: The deviation of the right lower lip when smiling is a characteristic finding in congenital unilateral lower lip palsy and isolated congenital facial paresis.
rationales.F04: Normal developmental milestones make Moebius syndrome less likely.
rationales.F07: Symmetric frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth suggest against Moebius syndrome.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of facial asymmetry with the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling or crying, while the rest of the facial movement is symmetric, are best explained by Congenital unilateral lower lip palsy, which directly addresses the specific finding of lower lip deviation without contradicting other normal developmental and examination findings.
